newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Krems to build resin plant in Hungary.
newsitem.headline: Krems to build resin plant in Hungary.

text.p: Austria's Krems Chemie AG will build a synthetic resin plant and together with chemicals firm Borsodchem a formaldehyde plant in Hungary , Borsodchem's president and chief executive Laszlo Kovacs told Reuters.
The synthetic resin plant will use the excess output of the formaldehyde plant, he said.
"Krems's (resin) factory will be operational in about a year," Kovacs said.
He confirmed earlier news that Borsodchem will build a 40,000 tonnes per year capacity formaldehyde plant of which it will use some 15,000 tonnes a year.
The one billion forints formaldehyde plant will be 30 percent owned by Krems and 70 percent by Borsodchem, Kovacs said.
Of the excess formaldehyde capacity, Krems will use 17,000 to 18,000 tonnes in its own synthetic resin plant, while the remaining roughly 10,000 tonnes will be sold in Hungary.
"Domestic formaldehyde demand is higher than that," Kovacs said.
Both the formaldehyde and the resin plants are expected to be operational within a year, Kovacs said.
